result.document_summary: A PublicCEO news article reporting that the Santa Ana City Council approved, on first reading on Feb. 17, 2026, an ordinance banning algorithmic rent-setting software for residential rentals, with a final vote set for March 3, 2026.
result.notes: The article is a secondary source and does not give the ordinance's municipal code citation or any effective date. It reports first-reading approval on Feb. 17 and a final vote set for March 3, 2026 but does not report the outcome of that final vote, so legal_state is recorded as pending (adoption not confirmed by this document). Coverage is limited to residential rental property within Santa Ana city limits. The article also mentions Santa Ana's existing rent stabilization ordinance only in passing, with no operative terms, so no rent_increase_limits or just_cause_eviction record was extracted.

rules.title: Santa Ana ban on algorithmic rent-setting software
rules.requirement: Prohibits the sale, licensing, provision and use of certain algorithmic rent-setting software for residential rental properties in Santa Ana. Tenants may sue directly and need only prove the landlord used the prohibited technology, not intentional collusion.
rules.key_value: Civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation, plus injunctive relief, damages and attorney's fees
rules.citation: Santa Ana algorithmic rent-setting software ordinance (first reading Feb. 17, 2026)
rules.quoted_span: prohibits the sale, licensing, provision and use of certain algorithmic rent-setting software for residential rental properties.
rules.coverage_text: Residential rental property within Santa Ana city limits.
rules.exemptions_text: Does not apply to pricing software that relies solely on publicly available data, aggregate historical data, or tools used to comply with affordable housing program requirements.
rules.interaction: Structured to operate alongside existing and proposed state antitrust laws while providing stronger local protections.
